title: Regular sequences and the canonical completed quotient presentation
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a finitely generated ideal, and put $B=R/I$. Let $\widehat R$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $R$ and let $\widehat B$ be the completion of $B$ at its maximal ideal. The canonical surjection $q:\widehat R\to\widehat B$ has the property that $I$ is generated by a finite $R$-regular sequence contained in $\mathfrak m$ if and only if $\ker q$ is generated by a finite $\widehat R$-regular sequence contained in the maximal ideal of $\widehat R$.

source.place: Tags 00MA (completion tensor), 00MB (completion flat), and 09Q1 setup; regularity of the completed local ring via More on Algebra Tag 07NY.

proof.text: Put $S=\widehat R$, let $c:R\to S$ be canonical, and put $J=IS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mS$ and residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Thus $S$ is nonzero, $c(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and $c$ induces the specified residue-field isomorphism. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, every generator $c(a)$ of $J$ lies in $\mathfrak n$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], the maximal ideal of $B=R/I$ is $\mathfrak m/I$; its $n$th power is the image of $\mathfrak m^n$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] gives the canonical coordinatewise map $q:S\to\widehat B$, its surjectivity, and $\ker q=J$.

source.place: Tags 05GI, 05GG, 0316, 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) and 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), applied to the finite module exact sequence for R/I.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-completed-ideal-generator-fibre], the completed inclusion identifies $I^\wedge$ with $J$, and $\beta:I/\mathfrak mI\xrightarrow{\sim}J/\mathfrak nJ$ sends the class of $a$ to the class of $c(a)$. The scalar field is the common residue field fixed in step 1.

source.place: Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), parts (2) and (3), and 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), applied to the inclusion of an arbitrary finite ideal and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: If $f_1,\ldots,f_t\in\mathfrak m$ regularly generate $I$, [lem-trf-completion-prefix-kernel-comparison] makes $c(f_1),\ldots,c(f_t)$ regular in $S$. They generate $J$: write each $a\in I$ as $\sum r_jf_j$, apply $c$, and take $S$-linear combinations. They lie in $\mathfrak n$ since $c(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Step 1 identifies their ideal with $\ker q$.

source.place: Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), part (2), applied to the kernel and image of each prefix multiplication; Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), and Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK) reflect a zero kernel. The quotient identifications use Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor).

proof.text: Conversely let $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathfrak n$ regularly generate $\ker q=J$. In [lem-trf-lift-regular-generators-through-fibre] take the Noetherian local rings $R,S$, the local map $c$ with residue-field isomorphism from step 1, the finite ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and the canonical generator-space isomorphism $\beta$ of step 2. It gives $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in I$ generating $I$ whose images are $S$-regular. These lifts lie in $\mathfrak m$, so [lem-trf-completion-prefix-kernel-comparison] reflects their regularity to $R$. This proves the converse. When $r=0$ the lifting lemma gives $I=0$, and the fixed-list lemma includes the empty regular sequence; the forward implication also includes the empty tuple.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (1), together with Algebra Tags 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), 061S (lemma-quasi-regular-regular), and 00DV (lemma-NAK); agent-formulated lifting consequence of a specified isomorphism on generator spaces.

lean.statement: theorem completionRegularKernelPreservation {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hIfg : I.FG) : let B := R ⧸ I let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R let n := Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) m let c := AdicCompletion.exists_local_completion_quotient R B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective) let q : AdicCompletion m R →+* AdicCompletion n B := c.2.choose Function.Surjective q ∧ ((∃ xs : List R, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R xs ∧ Ideal.ofList xs = I ∧ ∀ x ∈ xs, x ∈ m) ↔ (∃ ys : List (AdicCompletion m R), RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (AdicCompletion m R) ys ∧ Ideal.ofList ys = RingHom.ker q ∧ ∀ y ∈ ys, y ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion m R)))
lean.note: The completion ideal n is the image of the maximal ideal of R under R → R ⧸ I; under hI this is the maximal ideal of B. The chosen q is the canonical coordinatewise completion map supplied by AdicCompletion.exists_local_completion_quotient, whose witness includes surjectivity and kernel identification.
